messages:
Maria: Heads-up — I've been seeing steady memory growth on dedicated runners during long streaming toolloops (8-24h runs). Heap delta ~500-800MB over 12h on one box.
Owen: Repro steps? any flame graphs or heap profiles?
Maria: Minimal repro: run the toolloop harness with streaming enabled and prefix_cache disabled (we saw it faster without prefix cache). Command I used:
```
./ci/run_toolloop.sh --model rdx-small --stream --duration 12h --workers 2 --prefix-cache=false
```
Owen: ok, will spin one up.
perf-bot: nightly long-run profiler started: https://ci.redwood/prof/7893 (flamegraph + heapdiff attached)
Jess: I grabbed heap snapshots and traced growth to a PageMeta-ish object in the KV cache. Counts climb steadily only for long sessions; short chats show no leak.
Jess: Heap diff (abridged):
- PageMeta: +1200
- KVPageRef: +1200
- other small obj: +80

Stack samples point to two codepaths: fast-path eviction and a kernel-fallback path after kernel selection changed last week.
Tariq: We did change kernel selection heuristic for >512 seq to use fused attention kernel — that introduced a fallback path when runtime detects incompatible quant kernels. Could be a missing refcount decrement in the fallback.
Owen: Can you paste the stack traces?
Jess: gist: https://gist.redwood/p/trace123
Top frames:
- kv_page_pin_fastpath
- kernel_dispatch_fused
- kernel_dispatch_fallback
- kv_page_try_evict

Observation: when kernel_dispatch falls back, code takes an early return in the eviction fast-path and doesn't call kv_page_release() in one branch.
Maria: That matches my logs: periodic log lines "kv: fallback path took fast-exit, page still pinned" every ~5m across long runs.
Evan: If that's the case, trivial fix is to ensure any fast-exit runs through the common release path (finally-style). Can someone whip a minimal patch?
Jess: I'll prototype:
```c
// old
if (unlikely(kernel_fallback)) return -EAGAIN;
// new
if (unlikely(kernel_fallback)) {
  kv_page_unpin(page);
  return -EAGAIN;
}
```
Jess: Pushed branch: fix/kv-refcount-fallback. Ran local 24h run with prefix-cache=false and memory stayed flat.
Owen: Nice. Can we add an assertion in debug builds to catch imbalance? e.g., assert(kv_page_refcount(page) >= 0) and track total pinned pages metric.
Tariq: Yes — add a telemetry counter for "kv.page_ref_delta" and alert if delta > 200 in 1h on dedicated. Also add an eviction thrash detector when fallback rate > 5/min.
Evan: I'll open a canary rollout with the patch and the extra telemetry. Rolling to canary pool now — ETA 20m. @perf-bot please run the long-run regression job against canary. :rocket:
perf-bot: queued job 7900 on canary pool; will run 24h smoketest and post results.
Maria: One more note — the leak was much larger when prefix_cache was disabled; with prefix cache enabled the growth is slower because pages get reused more. So short-term mitigation: re-enable prefix cache for affected tenants while we roll the patch.
Jess: Filed INF-4521 and added reproducer + heap snapshots to the ticket.
Owen: After canary run, if successful, we should backport to the 2.14.x Dedicated patch branch (customers on pinned runtime).
Tariq: Also add a unit test that simulates kernel fallback during eviction and asserts refcount net zero.
Evan: Canary looks stable so far (2h in). Memory flat on the two canary boxes. Will promote to small prod cohort after 12h.
Maria: Thanks all — great catch. Leaving the original failing run up for now for postmortem data collection.
Jess: Follow-up actions in ticket: 1) merge patch + telemetry, 2) add unit test, 3) roll to prod cohort, 4) monitor kv.page_ref_delta alerting.
Owen: tl;dr: missing kv_page_unpin in kernel-fallback fast-path; patch validated in canary; rollback plan ready.
Maria: :thumbsup:
Evan: Closing loop — will post rollout timeline in #eng-releases when promoting.
perf-bot: job 7900 completed: no memory drift in 24h canary run; artifacts: https://ci.redwood/prof/7900
Maria: Marking this thread resolved pending prod cohort results.
